title: Staged-Channel Policy and Compatibility Grid for Serving & Client Surfaces
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Purpose: Define a pragmatic staged-channel policy and a cross-surface compatibility grid to ensure safe upgrades across the serving runtime, public API, SDKs, and Console. The goal is to make upgrade expectations explicit for both internal teams and customers so that we can run automated preflight checks and controlled rollouts with clear rollback criteria.

Scope: runtime (inference engine binary / model runtime), REST/SDK API surface, official SDKs (Python/TS/Go), and Redwood Console (observability + rollout controls). This doc prescribes: channel definitions, compatibility tiers, versioning conventions for each surface, automated preflight/compatibility tooling, rollout gate definitions, deprecation windows, and operational playbook for upgrades.

Channel taxonomy (recommended):
- experimental: daily builds, no compatibility promises, used for research and early dogfooding.
- beta: feature preview; best-effort compatibility for 1 minor; internal/external opt-in.
- stable: default channel for customers; API and SDK stability guarantees (no breaking API changes within a stable minor).
- lts: 12–18 month supported snapshots of stable with extended security/bugfix support and strict compatibility guarantees across runtime and client surfaces.

Compatibility tiers (how we label matrix entries):
- ABI-compatible: runtime binary changes that retain byte-level KV/cache layout and kernel contract; safe for in-place upgrade.
- API-compatible: HTTP/SDK contract unchanged; only additive fields allowed.
- PROTOCOL-compatible: wire-level changes that require client adapter but not full SDK bump.
- BREAKING: change requires major-version bump and migration steps.

Versioning conventions by surface (proposal):
- Runtime: semver-like but with ABI-protection policy. Format MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH where MAJOR increments for breaking ABI changes (very rare); MINOR for new features and performance improvements; PATCH for bugfixes. LTS pins a MINOR and receives only PATCH backports.
- API: MAJOR.MINOR where MINOR is used to gate non-breaking additions; MAJOR for breaking contract changes. A stable MINOR is supported for the lifetime of an LTS runtime pinned to it.
- SDKs: follow API MAJOR.MINOR and include an adapter shim to translate older runtime/API shapes for one MINOR back.
- Console: release channel aligned to API MINOR and includes feature-flags to gate UI changes; support window equals the LTS policy for the linked API/Runtime.

Compatibility Grid (operational rules):
- For an LTS runtime (R.x.y) we guarantee API compatibility with API.x for the lifetime of the LTS. SDKs versioned as SDK.x.y are guaranteed to be compatible with Runtime R.x.* and API.x.
- Backward compatibility is maintained across one previous MINOR for SDKs with the shim enabled.
- Runtime rolling upgrades within same MINOR are allowed on dedicated/dedicated-lite customers with preflight flags; cross-minor runtime upgrades require staged canary and explicit SDK compatibility verification.

Rollout gates and thresholds:
- Internal canary: 0.5% internal traffic for 6–12 hours; criteria: error-rate < 0.5x baseline, p95 latency within target, no regression on core eval prompts.
- External canary: 5% external traffic over 24h across 2 regions; additional checks against customer's pinned model/traffic shape.
- Regional ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% by region with 12-hour observation windows.
- Auto-rollback triggers: sustained error-rate > 2x baseline for 30m, latency p95 > x ms threshold, or quality regression score drop > configured threshold on evals.

Automated tooling (deliverables):
- compatibility-checker CLI: validates runtime-to-API contracts, SDK shims, and manifest compatibility (output = pass/warn/fail).
- preflight-runner job: executes smoke tests, end-to-end example prompts, and regression eval against the canary population.
- rollout-orchestrator: encodes gates, percentage ramps, and automatic rollback hooks tied to metrics in Console.
- binary-diff tool: highlights ABI-level changes and flags risky kernel switches.

Operational playbook highlights:
- PR flow: runtime / API / SDK changes MUST include compatibility-checker report.
- Release branch: LTS branches only accept PATCHes with required cherry-pick PRs and review by release-eng + security.
- Communication: announce LTS pinning and deprecation schedule 90 days ahead; provide migration doc and SDK migration helpers.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative LTS lifetime reduces upgrade burden for customers but increases maintenance burden for the platform team.
- One-MINOR shim for SDKs avoids breaking clients but may encourage complacency; plan periodic forced-adoption for major refactors.

Decision record: Recommend adopting the channel taxonomy and the tooling deliverables above. Pilot the compatibility-checker and preflight-runner in the next runtime minor release, and run 2 staged upgrades (internal and one partner) before the first official LTS pin.
